> **Which dwellings use the most gas and electricity, and how much do solar
> panels reduce the net electricity demand of a household?**

The analysis itself will run in CBS Remote Access. This page develops its
code on simulated `ENERGIEVERBRUIK` linked to the woonbase dwellings, and uses
StatLine 85140NED (energy use by dwelling characteristics) and 81528NED
(national averages) to show which simulated results look like the real ones.
Similar pages: `vignette("quality-cars")` and `vignette("quality-income")`.

## At a glance

::: {.glance}
| Result | Looks like reality? | In Remote Access |
|--------------------|----------|--------------|
| Gas by dwelling type, construction year, floor area | yes, within a few percent | similar; a large gap means a bug |
| Electricity by number of occupants | yes, about 5% high | similar |
| Solar panels by dwelling type; net electricity with and without | yes | similar |
| Percentiles of gas and electricity | yes | similar |
| National means per year | trend yes, a few percent low | similar |
| Combinations of characteristics (e.g. type by construction year) | not calibrated | can differ |
| Heating type, gas-free dwellings | codes consistent, shares assumed | can differ |
:::

Gas and electricity are generated per dwelling from its characteristics and
fitted to the one-way tables of 85140NED, so code for one-way breakdowns can
be checked against StatLine before it runs on the real data.

## Simulated data

```{r simulate}
sim_reset()
woonbase_init(year = 2023, n = 50000L, seed = 42L)
sim_init("energieverbruik", year = 2023, seed = 43L)

energie <- as.data.table(read_sav("ENERGIEVERBRUIK2023TABV1",
  col_select = c(RINOBJECTNUMMER, GASSJV, ELEK, ELEKTERUG, ELEKNETTO, ZONPV, GASBRON)))
# StatLine covers occupied dwellings: drop vacant ones (GASBRON LG)
energie <- energie[cbs_code(GASBRON) != "LG"]
woonr <- as.data.table(read_sav("WoonbasePopulatieWoonruimten2023V1",
  col_select = c(RINOBJECTNUMMER, VBOWoningType1Jan, AantalPersonenPerVSLKlasse1Jan)))
kenm <- as.data.table(read_sav("WoonbaseKenmerkenWoonruimten2023V1",
  col_select = c(RINOBJECTNUMMER, VBOBouwjaar1Jan, VBOOppervlakte1Jan)))

# GASSJV is temperature corrected, as in 85140NED
energie[, `:=`(gas = as.numeric(GASSJV), elek = as.numeric(ELEK),
               terug = as.numeric(ELEKTERUG), netto = as.numeric(ELEKNETTO),
               zon = cbs_code(ZONPV) == "1")]
energie[woonr, on = "RINOBJECTNUMMER", `:=`(
  woningtype = as.character(as_factor(i.VBOWoningType1Jan)),
  bewoners   = as.character(as_factor(i.AantalPersonenPerVSLKlasse1Jan)))]
energie[kenm, on = "RINOBJECTNUMMER", `:=`(
  bouwjaar = as.integer(i.VBOBouwjaar1Jan), oppervlak = as.numeric(i.VBOOppervlakte1Jan))]
```

The dwelling characteristics in the classes of 85140NED:

```{r classes}
BJ  <- c("voor 1946" = 1000, "1946-1964" = 1946, "1965-1974" = 1965, "1975-1991" = 1975,
         "1992-2005" = 1992, "2006-2014" = 2006, "2015 en later" = 2015)
OPP <- c("< 50 m2" = 2, "50-75 m2" = 50, "75-100 m2" = 75, "100-150 m2" = 100,
         "150-250 m2" = 150, ">= 250 m2" = 250)
energie[, `:=`(
  woningtype  = fcase(woningtype == "Vrijstaande woning", "Vrijstaande woning",
                      woningtype == "Twee-onder-een-kapwoning", "2-onder-1-kapwoning",
                      woningtype == "Hoekwoning", "Hoekwoning",
                      woningtype == "Tussenwoning", "Tussenwoning",
                      woningtype == "Meergezinswoning", "Appartement"),
  bouwjaar    = names(BJ)[findInterval(bouwjaar, BJ)],
  oppervlakte = names(OPP)[findInterval(oppervlak, OPP)],
  bewoners    = fifelse(bewoners %in% c("5", "6-9", ">=10"), "5 of meer", bewoners))]

by_kenmerk <- function(k) {
  energie[!is.na(get(k)), .(gas = mean(gas, na.rm = TRUE), elek = mean(elek, na.rm = TRUE),
                            zon = mean(zon) * 100),
          by = .(klasse = get(k))][, kenmerk := k]
}
sim_by <- rbindlist(lapply(c("woningtype", "bouwjaar", "oppervlakte", "bewoners"), by_kenmerk))
```

```{r statline, echo = FALSE}
sl <- statline("85140NED", Perioden = period(2023))
sl_trend <- statline("81528NED", RegioS = cbsodataR::has_substring("NL01"))
has_statline <- !is.null(sl) && !is.null(sl_trend)

DIMS <- c(woningtype = "Woningtype", bouwjaar = "Bouwjaar",
          oppervlakte = "Gebruiksoppervlakte", bewoners = "Bewonersklasse",
          zonnestroom = "HoofdverwarmingEnZonnestroom")
# rows of one dimension with every other dimension at its total
one_way <- function(dim) {
  keep <- rep(TRUE, nrow(sl))
  for (d in setdiff(DIMS, dim)) {
    lbl <- sl[[paste0(d, "_label")]]
    keep <- keep & grepl("^Totaal", lbl) & !grepl("met|zonder", lbl)
  }
  sl[keep]
}
# StatLine class labels mapped onto the simulated ones
sl_klasse <- function(k, lbl) {
  first <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(sub("^\\D*(\\d+).*$", "\\1", gsub(" ", "", lbl))))
  switch(k,
    woningtype  = lbl,
    bouwjaar    = names(BJ)[match(first, BJ)],
    oppervlakte = names(OPP)[match(first, OPP)],
    bewoners    = sub(" personen of meer", " of meer", sub(" perso(o|ne)n?$", "", lbl)))
}
sl_by <- if (has_statline) rbindlist(lapply(names(DIMS)[1:4], function(k) {
  d <- one_way(DIMS[[k]])
  d[, .(klasse = sl_klasse(k, get(paste0(DIMS[[k]], "_label"))),
        gas = measure(.SD, "^GemiddeldeAardgasleveringTempGecorr"),
        elek = measure(.SD, "^GemiddeldeElektriciteitslevering"),
        zon = measure(.SD, "^AandeelWoningenZonnestroomOpAdres"), kenmerk = k)][!is.na(klasse)]
}))
by_all <- rbindlist(list(sim_by[, bron := "simulatie"], sl_by[, bron := "StatLine"]),
                    use.names = TRUE)

# horizontal comparison of one measure by one characteristic
plot_by <- function(k, measure_col, levels, title, ylab, xlab, name) {
  d <- by_all[kenmerk == k & klasse %in% levels,
              .(klasse = factor(klasse, levels = levels), waarde = get(measure_col), bron)]
  p <- cpb_col(flip(d, "klasse"), x = klasse, y = waarde, fill = bron,
    colour_index = c(2, 6), position = "dodge", orientation = "horizontal",
    title = title, ylab = ylab, xlab = xlab)
  show_cpb(p, name)
}
TYPES <- c("Vrijstaande woning", "2-onder-1-kapwoning", "Hoekwoning", "Tussenwoning",
           "Appartement")
```

```{r statline-note, echo = FALSE, results = "asis", eval = run && !has_statline}
cat("> **Note.** StatLine could not be reached when this page was built, so",
    "only the simulated series are shown.\n")
```

## Gas by dwelling

```{r gas-plots, echo = FALSE}
plot_by("woningtype", "gas", TYPES, "Aardgasverbruik naar woningtype, 2023",
        "woningtype", "m3 per woning per jaar", "gas-type")
plot_by("bouwjaar", "gas", names(BJ), "Aardgasverbruik naar bouwjaar, 2023",
        "bouwjaar", "m3 per woning per jaar", "gas-bouwjaar")
plot_by("oppervlakte", "gas", names(OPP), "Aardgasverbruik naar oppervlakte, 2023",
        "gebruiksoppervlakte", "m3 per woning per jaar", "gas-oppervlakte")
```

The gradients are reproduced: a detached house uses more than twice the gas
of an apartment, the largest dwellings nearly four times the smallest, and
gas use falls steadily with the construction year.

## Electricity and solar panels

```{r solar}
energie[, .(netto = mean(netto, na.rm = TRUE), teruglevering = mean(terug, na.rm = TRUE)),
        by = .(zonnepanelen = zon)]
```

```{r elek-plots, echo = FALSE}
plot_by("bewoners", "elek", c("1", "2", "3", "4", "5 of meer"),
        "Elektriciteit naar bewoners, 2023", "aantal bewoners",
        "kWh per woning per jaar", "elek-bewoners")
plot_by("woningtype", "zon", TYPES, "Zonnepanelen naar woningtype, 2023",
        "woningtype", "% van de woningen", "zon-type")
zon <- rbindlist(list(
  energie[, .(netto = mean(netto, na.rm = TRUE), bron = "simulatie"),
          by = .(zonnepanelen = fifelse(zon, "met zonnepanelen", "zonder zonnepanelen"))],
  if (has_statline) one_way("HoofdverwarmingEnZonnestroom")[
    grepl("^Totaal (met|zonder) zonnestroom", HoofdverwarmingEnZonnestroom_label),
    .(zonnepanelen = fifelse(grepl("zonder", HoofdverwarmingEnZonnestroom_label),
                             "zonder zonnepanelen", "met zonnepanelen"),
      netto = measure(.SD, "^NettoElektriciteitsleveringGemiddelde"), bron = "StatLine")]),
  use.names = TRUE)
p <- cpb_col(zon, x = zonnepanelen, y = netto, fill = bron,
  position = "dodge", reverse_legend = FALSE,
  title = "Netto elektriciteitslevering, 2023", ylab = "kWh per woning per jaar")
show_cpb(p, "netto")
```

Electricity rises with the number of occupants, a few percent high in every
group. Solar panels follow the published shares per dwelling type, and net
electricity of dwellings with panels is half that of dwellings without, as
published.

## Distribution and trend

```{r percentiles}
sim_pct <- energie[, .(percentiel = seq(10, 90, 10),
                       aardgas = quantile(gas, seq(0.1, 0.9, 0.1), na.rm = TRUE),
                       elektriciteit = quantile(elek, seq(0.1, 0.9, 0.1), na.rm = TRUE))]
```

```{r distribution-plots, echo = FALSE, out.width = "700px"}
sl_pct <- if (has_statline) {
  tot <- one_way("none")
  data.table(percentiel = seq(10, 90, 10),
    aardgas = vapply(seq(10, 90, 10), function(p)
      measure(tot, paste0("^AardgasTempGecorrPercentiel", p, "_")), numeric(1)),
    elektriciteit = vapply(seq(10, 90, 10), function(p)
      measure(tot, paste0("^ElektriciteitsleveringPercentiel", p, "_")), numeric(1)))
}
pct <- melt(rbindlist(list(sim_pct[, bron := "simulatie"], sl_pct[, bron := "StatLine"]),
                      use.names = TRUE),
            id.vars = c("percentiel", "bron"), variable.name = "drager", value.name = "verbruik")
p <- cpb_line(lines_bron(pct), x = percentiel, y = verbruik, colour = bron,
  colour_index = c(6, 2), points = TRUE,
  facet = drager, facet_scales = "free_y",
  title = "Verdeling energieverbruik per woning, 2023",
  ylab = "m3 of kWh per woning per jaar", xlab = "percentiel")
show_cpb(p, "percentielen", page = "full")

trend_sim <- rbindlist(lapply(2015:2024, function(y) {
  sim_reset()
  woonbase_init(year = y, n = 10000L, seed = 42L)
  sim_init("energieverbruik", year = y, seed = 43L)
  e <- as.data.table(read_sav(sprintf("ENERGIEVERBRUIK%dTABV1", y),
                              col_select = c(GAS, ELEK, GASBRON)))[cbs_code(GASBRON) != "LG"]
  data.table(jaar = y, gas = mean(as.numeric(e$GAS), na.rm = TRUE),
             elek = mean(as.numeric(e$ELEK), na.rm = TRUE),
             bron = "simulatie")
}))
trend_sl <- if (has_statline) {
  sl_trend[Woningkenmerken_label == "Totaal woningen",
           .(jaar = as.integer(Perioden_label), gas = measure(.SD, "^GemiddeldAardgasverbruik"),
             elek = measure(.SD, "^GemiddeldeElektriciteitslevering"), bron = "StatLine")][
    jaar %in% 2015:2024]
}
trend <- melt(rbindlist(list(trend_sim, trend_sl), use.names = TRUE),
              id.vars = c("jaar", "bron"), variable.name = "drager", value.name = "verbruik")
trend[, drager := factor(fifelse(drager == "gas", "aardgas (m3)", "elektriciteit (kWh)"))]
p <- cpb_line(lines_bron(trend), x = jaar, y = verbruik, colour = bron,
  colour_index = c(6, 2), points = TRUE,
  facet = drager, facet_scales = "free_y",
  title = "Gemiddeld energieverbruik per woning", ylab = "per woning per jaar")
show_cpb(p, "trend", page = "full")
```

Both distributions follow the published percentiles, including the tenth of
dwellings without gas (district heating, most new dwellings, other
all-electric homes). The national means follow the published trend a few
percent low: the model matches the mean *within* each dwelling group, and the
simulated stock has relatively more small, low-use dwellings.

## Before you move to Remote Access

The simulated file follows the rules of the real one, so the code above
already deals with them:

- **Empty values.** `GAS` and `ELEK` are empty where delivery was not
  assigned (`GASBRON` NT), so every mean and quantile uses `na.rm = TRUE`.
- **Vacant dwellings** have no gas and no electricity (`GASBRON` LG) and are
  dropped, as StatLine covers occupied dwellings.
- **Net electricity** is `ELEK - ELEKTERUG` capped at 0, with feed-in capped
  at twice delivery; recompute it the same way or use `ELEKNETTO`.
- **Variables from 2022.** `ZONPVBRON` and `KBHOOFDVERWARMING31DEC` are empty
  in earlier years.

What still differs is content: combinations of characteristics that the
one-way StatLine tables do not pin down.
